# Ahmed Mohammed — AI/ML Engineer

## Key Achievements

- 99.03% ± 0.07% average AUROC on CIFAR-10 airplane-vs-rest (binary, single ID class, 3-seed mean; not comparable to multi-class CIFAR-10 OOD leaderboards) — Master's Thesis, JKU Linz (graded 1), 2026
- Introduced class-conditional separation loss improving OOD AUROC to 99.03% ± 0.07% (3-seed mean; +6.5 percentage points over 92.52% ± 11.07% baseline, dramatically reducing cross-seed standard deviation)
- 0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC baseline on the public FTI_Zer0P industrial defect benchmark under strict 5-fold CV (PROFACTOR GmbH / JKU Linz, Zer0P)

## Projects

- [OOD Detection Framework](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/DiffusionOOD): Novel use of conditional diffusion models as generative classifiers for out-of-distribution detection. 99.03% ± 0.07% average AUROC on CIFAR-10 airplane-vs-rest (binary, single ID class, 3-seed mean). Introduced class-conditional separation loss. Applied to industrial quality control via a Stage-1 YOLOv8m detector (6,408 128×128 YOLO crops across 573 source-image groups) plus multi-head conditional diffusion on the public FTI_Zer0P benchmark (0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC, 5-fold CV; thesis-documented).
- Thesis PDF erratum: the thesis text identifies the detector as YOLOv8n; the trained artifact yolo_best.pt is YOLOv8m (25.86M params, verified from train_args).
- [Industrial Anomaly Detection](https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Diffusion-Based%20Multi-class%20Defect%20Detection.pdf): Early 2024 YOLO + diffusion model pipeline for industrial defect detection — a negative-result technical report that motivated the later thesis approach. (The FTI_Zer0P 0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC baseline under 5-fold CV is reported in the [Master's thesis](https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Mohammed_Ahmed_Thesis_Diffusion_OOD_Detection.pdf), not this report.)
- [Sihem](https://sihem-pwa.pages.dev/): Independent personal-mentor project with an invitation-only beta on Telegram and the installable web app. The native Android client uses Kotlin and Jetpack Compose and is in private testing. Built on Supabase edge functions (Deno/TS) with pgvector RAG long-term memory, multi-provider LLM routing (GLM/Gemini/Groq) with failover, a deterministic generators-arbiter-composer decision engine, multimodal meal-photo vision, TTS voice reminders, and Google Calendar sync (@sihem_ai_bot). Includes an interactive 3-scenario illustrative walkthrough of the invitation-only beta at https://ahmed-3m.github.io/case-studies/sihem/.
- [mergeproof](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/mergeproof): Checks AI-written pull requests against configured deterministic merge requirements without calling an LLM. Passing those checks does not guarantee defect-free code. Zero dependencies, MIT, npm package @ahmed-3m/mergeproof. Also available as a live client-side interactive PR gate playground (0 LLM calls) in the portfolio Projects section (`https://ahmed-3m.github.io/?view=full#mergeproof-playground`) and concise work rail.
- [EEG Signal Classification](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/Motor-Imagery-classification): LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU architectures for EEG motor imagery classification in brain-computer interface applications. Hyperparameter optimization across architectures (Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences, 2023).
- [Elbostan Pazar bot](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/Elbostan-Pazar-bot): Messenger bot that answers a real shop's customers about prices, hours and delivery.
- [brainstorm2idea](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/brainstorm2idea) + [idea2prototype](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/idea2prototype): zero-dependency tools that take a fuzzy idea to a linted brief, then to a tested prototype, with any coding agent.

## Full Blog Post Content

### Blog: Deterministic Guardrails for LLM and Agent Systems: Sihem's Arbiter and mergeproof
URL: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/blog/deterministic-guardrails-for-llm-and-agent-systems/
Date: 2026-11-25
Tags: Agentic AI, LLM Systems, Deterministic Guardrails, Sihem, mergeproof, Supabase

Across both Sihem and mergeproof, probabilistic models stay inside the synthesis layer while deterministic code owns state, scheduling, and policy verification.

Sihem (accepted into the tech2b incubator in Linz; running in invitation-only beta via Telegram bot @sihem_ai_bot and installable PWA at https://sihem-pwa.pages.dev/, with a Kotlin/Jetpack Compose Android client in private testing) separates proactive outreach into generators → arbiter → composer. Scheduled pg_cron jobs inspect activities and Google Calendar sync to propose candidates; deterministic TypeScript rules inside Deno / Supabase Edge Functions backed by PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security enforce quiet windows, cooldowns, and user isolation before any LLM is called; the composer then retrieves pgvector RAG long-term memory and routes across GLM, Gemini, and Groq with escalation and failover (plus optional Cloudflare MeloTTS voice notes). Generated text still requires validation and may contain errors, and the beta focuses on ongoing product validation without claiming measured user outcome gains.

mergeproof (https://github.com/ahmed-3m/mergeproof, npm @ahmed-3m/mergeproof, zero dependencies, MIT license) applies the same boundary to coding-agent pull requests: it validates AI-written diffs against configured deterministic merge requirements (such as flagging modified existing tests for human review) with 0 LLM calls. Passing deterministic checks does not guarantee defect-free code.

### Blog: How I Reached 99.03% ± 0.07% AUROC (3-seed mean) on OOD Detection with Conditional Diffusion Models
URL: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/blog/ood-diffusion-thesis/
Date: 2026-07-12
Tags: Diffusion Models, OOD Detection, Deep Learning, PyTorch, CIFAR-10, Generative Models, JKU Linz

My Master's thesis at JKU Linz (under Prof. Sepp Hochreiter) introduced class-conditional separation loss into conditional diffusion models used as generative classifiers — achieving an average of 99.03% ± 0.07% AUROC on CIFAR-10 airplane-vs-rest (binary, single ID class, 3-seed mean), stable over seeds and showing a +6.5pp gain over the non-separated baseline ($92.52\% \pm 11.07\%$).

Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is the ability of a neural network to say "I don't know" when it sees something it was never trained on. My key contribution was a class-conditional separation loss λ·L_sep that explicitly pushes the model's conditional noise predictions ε_θ(x_t, t, c=0) and ε_θ(x_t, t, c=1) apart during training, widening the reconstruction-error gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution inputs.

Ablation results on CIFAR-10 (average across seeds):
- λ=0.0 (baseline): 92.52% ± 11.07% AUROC (degenerate on SVHN OOD due to unstable scores)
- λ=0.001: 97.32% (seed-42)
- λ=0.01: 98.82% ± 0.06%
- λ=0.02 (best): 99.03% ± 0.07% (3-seed mean; seed-42 achieved 98.98% within-CIFAR, 90.50%–96.97% zero-shot across external sets)
- λ=0.05: 98.51% (seed-42)
- λ=0.1: 96.67% (seed-42)

The reported thesis result of 99.03% ± 0.07% AUROC (3-seed mean) is the average performance across seeds, with seed-42 achieving 90.50% to 96.97% zero-shot generalization across five external reproducible benchmarks (CIFAR-100, Places365, FashionMNIST, Textures, SVHN).

Applied to industrial data under strict 5-fold cross-validation on the public FTI_Zer0P dataset, the YOLO+CDM crop-based baseline (λ = 0.0) reaches 0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC. Separation loss weights do not significantly improve performance (p-values > 0.05 after Holm correction), illustrating a critical boundary condition. This domain-dependent cross-domain analysis is a key thesis contribution.

Implementation: PyTorch + PyTorch Lightning, DDPM U-Net with class conditioning, Hydra + Weights & Biases, trained on JKU GPU cluster (RTX A6000).

Open-sourced at github.com/ahmed-3m/DiffusionOOD. Full thesis PDF: ahmed-3m.github.io/Mohammed_Ahmed_Thesis_Diffusion_OOD_Detection.pdf

### Blog: Diffusion Models for Industrial Defect Detection at PROFACTOR GmbH
URL: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/blog/diffusion-models-anomaly-detection/
Date: 2024-11-20
Tags: Diffusion Models, Anomaly Detection, YOLOv8, Industrial AI, Computer Vision, Quality Control

Working with PROFACTOR GmbH (Steyr, Austria; remote / home office) through the JKU Institute for Machine Learning, I evaluated a machine vision pipeline for defect detection on inkjet-printed building components as part of Zer0P — a zero-defect manufacturing initiative funded by the Government of Upper Austria.

Architecture: Two-stage YOLO + conditional diffusion pipeline on FTI_Zer0P. Stage 1 uses a YOLOv8m detector (25.86M params in the released yolo_best.pt checkpoint; the thesis text identifies the detector as YOLOv8n) to localize 8 printed feature types (angle, dist1, dist6, dots, edge1-4) and extract 6,408 128×128 RGB crops across 573 source-image groups. Stage 2 uses a multi-head conditional diffusion U-Net (NoisePredictorV3 with AdaGN conditioning across the 8 feature types) as a generative classifier.

Results by feature type under 5-fold CV baseline (λ = 0.0, K=100): dots 0.9557 ± 0.0353 AUROC, dist6 0.9362 ± 0.0666. Overall baseline AUROC is 0.8673 ± 0.0230 (accuracy 0.8094 ± 0.0151, FPR@95%TPR 0.5631 ± 0.1697) under strict 5-fold image-level CV. Separation loss weights (λ ∈ {0.01, 0.02, 0.05}) produce AUROC scores within the cross-fold standard deviation (e.g. 0.8670 ± 0.0256 at λ = 0.05), which are statistically non-significant after Holm correction (adjusted p > 0.05).

Key lessons: (1) Generative models vs discriminative baselines in scarce-defect settings, (2) Feature type heterogeneity matters more than architecture, (3) Statistical rigor with 5-fold image-level CV + Holm correction is non-negotiable, (4) Domain gains on semantic natural images do not automatically transfer to small industrial feature crops.

Benchmark source (M.Sc. thesis): https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Mohammed_Ahmed_Thesis_Diffusion_OOD_Detection.pdf

Early technical report (2024, negative result): https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Diffusion-Based%20Multi-class%20Defect%20Detection.pdf

Industrial dataset: https://zenodo.org/records/11444566 (FTI_Zer0P Dataset 2023, Profactor GmbH, CC-BY-4.0)

---

### Blog: YOLOv8 for Industrial Quality Control: Decisions That Actually Moved the Needle
URL: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/blog/computer-vision-yolo-mastery/
Date: 2024-10-20
Tags: Computer Vision, YOLOv8, Deep Learning, Industrial AI, PyTorch, Production ML

Engineering notes on Stage-1 feature localization, image-level data splits, and evaluation trade-offs from the industrial inkjet quality-control benchmark (0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC under 5-fold CV on FTI_Zer0P).

Key decisions:
1. Two-stage YOLOv8m detector + conditional diffusion pipeline: Stage 1 uses a YOLOv8m detector (640×640 input, 25.86M params in yolo_best.pt; the thesis text identifies the detector as YOLOv8n) to localize 8 structured print feature types from 1920×1080 frames and extract 128×128 RGB crops for Stage 2 generative classification.
2. Data & leakage control: 6,408 128×128 YOLO crops across 573 source-image groups on public FTI_Zer0P (8 feature types), split at the source-image level so crops from the same print never leak across folds. Crops are resized to 128×128 without synthetic crop augmentation.
3. Training & architecture: reproducible PyTorch Lightning + Hydra configs training a multi-head conditional diffusion U-Net (NoisePredictorV3 with AdaGN feature-type embeddings) across all 8 feature heads.
4. Evaluation: 5-fold stratified image-level CV, AUROC as primary metric (0.8673 ± 0.0230 baseline at λ = 0.0, K=100), with per-feature breakdown showing stronger separation on Dots (0.9557 ± 0.0353) and Distance 6 (0.9362 ± 0.0666) than sparse Edge/Angle classes.
5. Engineering lesson: isolating Stage-1 detection from Stage-2 anomaly scoring keeps per-feature diagnostics, threshold calibration, and cross-domain validation transparent without conflating internal runtime targets with public benchmark AUROC.

What I'd do differently: (1) Collect more BAD samples for rare feature classes like Angle, (2) Quantify Stage-1 detector miss impact alongside Stage-2 crop scoring, (3) Track every ablation run with Hydra + W&B from day one.
